filament.name: Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA

heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S can reliably process Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA up to a safe maximum speed of 155 mm/s constrained by a 13 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. However, printing this abrasive composite requires replacing the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears with hardened steel components to avoid rapid wear.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a protective release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 13 mm³/s under the Filament profile to enforce the 155 mm/s maximum linear speed ceiling.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2 mm to prevent stringing and clumping common with carbon fiber-loaded melt pools.
Set the Top Glass / Front Door status note or crack the chamber door open to prevent heat creep with low-Tg PLA matrices.
Adjust Pressure Advance (PA) to 0.024-0.028 to maintain crisp corners despite the increased viscosity from carbon fiber milling.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Carbon fiber particles clogging in a worn stock 0.4mm stainless steel nozzle or heat creep caused by an enclosed chamber printing PLA.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Upgrade to a 0.4mm or 0.6mm hardened steel hotend, upgrade to hardened extruder gears, and vent the top glass or leave the door ajar during printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The abrasive carbon fiber particles rapidly enlarged the stock stainless steel nozzle orifice beyond 0.4mm.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Swap out the worn nozzle assembly for an official Bambu Lab hardened steel hotend and recalibrate flow dynamics.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough Surface Texture and Excessive Brittle Layer Separation
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Wet filament causing steam voids during extrusion, exacerbated by high part cooling preventing fiber entanglement.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry filament at 50°C for 6 hours in an active dryer, and cap maximum part cooling fan speed to 80%.

faq.question: Can I print Proto-pasta HTPLA-CF using the stock Bambu P1S stainless steel nozzle?
faq.answer: No, carbon fiber fibers are highly abrasive and will erode the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears in less than one spool, degrading print quality and causing clogs.

faq.question: Should I keep the P1S door and top lid fully closed for Proto-pasta HTPLA-CF?
faq.answer: No, because HTPLA has a standard PLA base with a low glass transition temperature (~55-60°C), an enclosed chamber can cause heat creep and extruder jams; prop the door open or vent the top glass.

faq.question: Does Proto-pasta HTPLA-CF work reliably with the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, but because the fibers make the filament more brittle and abrasive, ensure the spool rolls freely, and upgrade to hardened steel extruder feeder funnels if running extensive quantities.

faq.question: How do I anneal Proto-pasta HTPLA to achieve its high-temp resistance on the P1S?
faq.answer: Bake the finished print in an oven or on the P1S heated bed at 110°C for 30–60 minutes; account for roughly 1-2% shrinkage in X/Y and 1% expansion in Z by scaling the model in OrcaSlicer beforehand.
